Medhātithi
------------------------------------------
The Manusmṛti is, perhaps, one of the most ancient and authoritative works in the dharmaśāstra literature. The earliest and exhaustive commentary on it is the bhāṣya of मेधातिथि. Circumstantial evidence as gleaned from other works of dharmaśāstra points to the period A.

-900 as his probable period.
The Manusmṛti with the bhāṣya of मेधातिथि has been published three or four times.
Nothing is known of मेधातिथि. Some scholars feel that he belonged to South India while others assert that he hailed from Kashmir.
He seems to have been a deep scholar of पूर्वमीमाṁसा system and quotes numerous writers of an earlier period such as गौतम, आपस्तम्ब, बौधायन, वसिष्ठ, पराशर, बृहस्पति and others. He has drawn upon the Arthaśāstra of कौटिल्य (321-300 B. C.) in numerous places as also the sūtras of पाणिनि (400 B. C.) and the bhāṣya of पतञ्जलि (200 B. C.).
He also brings in several न्यायस् or maxims for explaining Manusmṛti, like the Kākatālīyanyāya (on 1.12) and Viśvajit-nyāya (on 2.2).
It is interesting to note that the text of the Manusmṛti on which he has commented is practically the same as we have now.

Medhāsūkta
(‘hymn of Medhā, the goddess of comprehension’)
------------------------------------------
To understand the correct meaning of the scriptures, power of intellect and comprehension as also retention in memory are very necessary. All these are reflected in that one wonderful word ‘medhāśakti’. Medhā has been conceived in the वेदस् as a goddess presiding over the power of memory and understanding.
There are two Medhāsūktas available now. The first is a खिल, addendum, occurring at the end of Śraddhāsūkta (Ṛgveda 10.151). The second forms a part of the Taittirīya Āraṇyaka (10.39.42) and occurs in the body of the Mahānārāyaṇa Upaniṣad (43). It is a short hymn of only five mantras.
A free translation of these verses can now be given:
May the all-penetrating goddess of intellect (Medhādevī) who is auspicious, well-disposed towards us, delighted with us come to us. May we, who were delighting in profitless speech before your visit, be now blessed by you, become enlightened and speak—along with our heroic progeny—forcefully expressing the Supreme Truth.
O Medhādevi! Favoured by you, one becomes a ṛṣi (seer), a ब्राह्मण (knower of ब्रह्मन्) or a possessor of riches, of various types. O goddess of intellect! Kindly bless us with the best of wealth.
May इन्द्र grant me intelligence. May the goddess सरस्वती grant me intelligence. May the twins, the अश्विन्स्, wearing garlands of lotus, generate intelligence in me.
May that Medhādevī who resides in the apsaras (celestial maidens), who is the mental power of the गन्धर्वस् (a type of demi-gods), who is the Vedic lore (Sarasvatī) belonging to the gods, who spreads like fragrance, favour me!
That Medhā (the goddess of intelligence) who is fragrant, who is of the form of retention in memory of all śāstras, who is of golden hue, who is pervading the world, who is fit to be resorted to by the seekers, who is full of strength, who nourishes us by milk, may she come to me with a joyful face and favour me.
